items.author: ragesoss

identitySources.claim: The photographer identifies the supermarket specimen as a Lady Alice apple; the original photograph is licensed CC BY-SA 3.0.
The grower's apple catalog separately lists the Lady Alice cultivar.

items.reviewBasis: Inspected the original 2448 by 3264 photograph. One unobstructed round apple is held in a hand; its red-pink blush, yellow background, stem depression, and pale speckling are clearly visible. Exact cultivar attribution comes from the photographer. No checkout number is visible. PC remains only the workbook qualifier, and the photographer's organic description is not transferred to the target catalog record. Only one distinct source photograph was found; any role reuse must remain explicit.

visibleIdentity.label: Lady Alice apple
visibleIdentity.cue: Look for a round apple with a red-pink blush over yellow skin and a shallow stem depression.

queries: Lady Alice PC apple Round apple (prior discovery)
rejections: Historical books containing a person or rose named Lady Alice were irrelevant. The Commons Lady Alice apple category contains only this one photograph.

identitySources.claim: The supplier-provided product description equates Goldendew with golden honeydew/Dewlicious. This supports the expanded search term, not a license for its product photograph.
The retailer lists Golden Dew and shows a whole smooth yellow melon.

items.reviewBasis: Expanded the source name to golden honeydew and examined the Commons candidate at original resolution. Its small-looking elongated yellow fruits have conspicuous narrow white longitudinal stripes; this conflicts with the retailer's smooth unstriped Golden Dew appearance. The caption alone is insufficient to admit that candidate. Need a photograph explicitly identified as the catalog's Goldendew/golden honeydew with compatible pixels and reuse rights.

rejections.reason: Pixel-reviewed CC0 image has yellow elongated fruit with strong white stripes, which does not safely match the Golden Dew supplier references. Do not use its filename as proof of cultivar identity.
Product identity lead; no grant to republish the retailer photograph was established.

identitySources.claim: The grower identifies Honey Kiss as its Chinese melon variety and supplies a specific product photograph.
The distributor describes Honey Kiss as an oblong Chinese Golden Hami melon, supporting Hami as a related source-search term.

items.reviewBasis: Searched both joined and separated Honeykiss/Honey Kiss spellings, then examined three rights-compatible Hami photographs. They show recognizable melons but neither their metadata nor visible packaging establishes Honey Kiss. The grower has the exact photograph but its page does not grant image reuse. Need permission for that exact image or another photographer's explicitly identified Honey Kiss specimen.
queries: Honey Kiss melon creative commons photo

rejections.reason: Exact grower identity, but copyright is reserved and no photo reuse grant was established.
Inspected original photograph: loose yellow netted melons with no Honey Kiss label. Metadata identifies only Hami.
Inspected original photograph: orange-yellow netted melon with no Honey Kiss label. Metadata identifies only Hami.
Inspected original photograph: a market group of green/yellow netted Hami melons beside other produce. No exact Honey Kiss identity evidence.

identitySources.claim: The retailer labels the product Meridol and lists its ingredient as Maradol Papaya, directly connecting the two spellings.
The supplier's Meridol product page describes the supplied fruit as Maradol papaya, providing a second spelling bridge.
The photographer explicitly identifies the real supermarket fruit as Maradol and releases the image under CC0.

items.reviewBasis: The Meridol/Maradol spelling connection is now supported by two direct product suppliers. The original Commons image clearly shows elongated green-yellow papayas, but both prominent stickers print checkout code 4395, while this catalog teaches 3112. That image would introduce conflicting checkout evidence. Need a different verified Maradol photograph without the competing code or a separately reviewed lawful presentation that removes the conflicting sticker without falsely changing the fruit.

rejections.reason: Original image inspected; prominent stickers state 4395, conflicting with workbook code 3112. Rejected as the unmodified lesson image despite correct identity and CC0 rights.
The CC BY research source concerns fresh-cut experimental papaya and does not establish a suitable whole-fruit recognition photograph in the searched evidence.

identitySources.claim: CFIA records the Taylors Gold pear denomination and provides a named comparison photograph with Comice and Bosc.
The direct produce supplier identifies Taylor's Gold and its distinct russeted Comice-derived identity.

items.reviewBasis: Expanded Taylor Gold to Taylor's Gold and Taylors Gold. Found exact cultivar photographs at CFIA, IP Australia, and a commercial photographer, but no clearly reusable standalone photograph was established. CFIA's comparison contains three varieties; its reproduction policy also distinguishes unaltered noncommercial use. IP Australia's general license excludes third-party supplied content, leaving plant-applicant photograph rights unresolved. Need a standalone licensed target photo or permission from its owner.

rejections.reason: Exact source lead, but comparison image includes two other cultivars and standalone/altered image reuse rights were not established. Policy: https://inspection.canada.ca/en/about-cfia/applying-crown-copyright

Exact cultivar photo found, but the applicant-supplied photo's reuse rights were not established. The general policy at https://www.ipaustralia.gov.au/about-us/about-this-site/copyright excludes third-party material.
Exact cultivar photograph requires purchasing a license; no purchase was made.

rejections: Commons Taylor searches returned historical book authors and unrelated names; generic Comice or Bosc is not substituted for Taylor's Gold.

identitySources.claim: The nursery sells the named Vaniglia persimmon cultivar, providing a targeted identity/source lead.
A second nursery lists Diospyros kaki Vaniglia.

items.reviewBasis: Expanded the media search to Italian Vaniglia, kaki, and persimmon. Exact cultivar photographs were found on nursery and stock-image pages, but a photo license was not established. Search hits licensed under Creative Commons either showed vanilla beans/oranges, scientific diagrams, or unrelated fruit. The catalog's English Vanilla also needs an explicit documented link to the selected Vaniglia specimen before a future promotion.

rejections.reason: Metadata explicitly identifies vanilla orchid beans, not persimmon.
Exact cultivar stock-photo lead requires a license; no purchase was made.

rejections: No suitable real fruit photograph with an established reuse license was found in the bounded search; generic Fuyu and Hachiya photographs are not cultivar substitutes.

identitySources.claim: The nursery's Vaniglia persimmon is a cultivar lead shared with the loose Vanilla catalog row.
A second nursery lists Diospyros kaki Vaniglia.

items.reviewBasis: This case record shares the unresolved cultivar-photo search with persimmons-vanilla. A future exact licensed cultivar photograph can support label-assisted learning, keeping Case and code 71207 tied to the workbook. No actual case configuration or quantity was inferred from loose fruit or nursery photographs.
rejections: The same exact-cultivar license and English-name linkage gaps recorded for persimmons-vanilla apply here.
Generic persimmon crates do not establish the Vanilla cultivar, and a loose fruit photograph cannot demonstrate a case's quantity.

items.author: Cs california

identitySources.claim: The direct supplier labels Sher Li Hon with the Chinese name 雪里紅 and identifies it as a mustard green.
The Chinese Agricultural Museum identifies 雪菜, 雪里蕻, and 雪里红 as names of the same branching mustard vegetable, connecting the supplier name to the photograph's metadata.
The grower labels Sher-Li-Hon as small Chinese mustard green and describes broad green leaves with ribbed green stems.
The original photograph is explicitly identified as Brassica juncea snow mustard (雪里蕻) and is licensed CC BY 4.0.

items.reviewBasis: Inspected the original 2268 by 4032 photograph. Raw green leaf blades, serrated margins, pale midribs, and attached stems are clearly visible. The exact name bridge is supplier Sher Li Hon/雪里紅, agricultural museum 雪里红/雪里蕻, then photographer snow mustard/雪里蕻. The photograph depicts a growing plant; it supports leaf and stem recognition, with no claim that a harvested bunch, retail unit, or package is shown. Only one distinct source photograph was found; any role reuse must remain explicit.

visibleIdentity.label: Sher-Li-Hon snow mustard
visibleIdentity.form: Broad serrated leaves and green stems
visibleIdentity.cue: Look for broad green leaves with serrated edges and pale ribs running into the stems.

queries: 雪里蕻 雪里红 site:gov.cn
rejections: Prior discovery lacked a product-head vocabulary for Sher-Li-Hon. Native-name search supplies the missing source link.
Generic mustard-green photographs were not selected because they do not establish the specific snow-mustard identity.

identitySources.claim: UF/IFAS describes the exact Fallglo tangerine cultivar and explicitly captions Figure 1 as Fallglo; image credit is UF/IFAS CREC.
USDA distinguishes Fallglo from the related US Early Pride cultivar; similar appearance does not make the cultivars interchangeable.

items.reviewBasis: The exact cultivar reference and figure exist at UF/IFAS. Its copyright page explicitly excludes individual article images from the document's Creative Commons license, so that figure cannot be admitted on the document license alone. Commons and USDA search produced no independently licensed exact whole-fruit photograph. Need permission for the UF/IFAS CREC image or another exact Fallglo source.

rejections.reason: Figure is credited UF/IFAS CREC. https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/copyright explicitly says the document license does not apply to individual images.
The citrus spread mentions Sunburst and Fallglo but does not identify the background photograph as an exact Fallglo specimen.

rejections: US Early Pride, Sunburst, and generic tangerine images are not substituted for Fallglo.

identitySources.claim: The photographer names a Mickey Lee watermelon purchased from Alexander Farms; the photo is explicitly a composite of the same specimen before and after cutting.
The Watermelon Board groups Mickey Lee/Sugarbaby under PLU 4331. A shared code does not establish that the two cultivars are visually identical.

items.reviewBasis: Located a photographer's exact Mickey Lee specimen and a University of Costa Rica research-image lead. The Flickr photo is all rights reserved; the research-image page says its content may be subject to copyright and did not establish a reusable source license. Commons found no exact Mickey Lee watermelon photograph. Need a licensed photograph of Mickey Lee itself; the shared 4331 code is not enough to relabel Sugar Baby images.
queries: Mickey Lee Watermelon from Alexander Farms

rejections.reason: Exact specimen but all rights reserved; photograph is also an acknowledged composite, not three independent observations.
Exact university research-image lead, but no reuse license was established.

rejections: Generic striped watermelon, Sugar Baby, and Mickey Lee Gold F1 are not exact replacements for the named Mickey Lee target.
